newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds seesaw in mixed, cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds seesaw in mixed, cautious trade.

text.p: Trade in Irish government bonds was mixed on Monday with shorter-dated stock losing ground while 10-year paper edged up in cautious trade amidst concern over domestic political unease and fallout from overseas data.
"German bunds have succumbed to modest profit-taking while UK gilts edged up after the UK November PMI data," one dealer said.
UK PMI came in at 54.4 percent compared with forecasts of 52.9 percent and against 54.5 percent previously.
By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 shed five pence from Friday's close to 102.70 to yield 5.76 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 added 15 pence to 110.45 to yield 6.40 percent.

Dealers said Irish pound strength against the German mark had put some bid interest into the market and a close eye was likely to be kept on the currency while the punt hovered close to 2.600 marks, its highest levels versus that currency since early 1993.
U.S. NAPM data, which was slightly stronger than expected, caused some weakness in the U.S. market, dealers said.

"The NAPM came in above 50 which suggests that output is expanding but on the positive side the prices balance was weak as was the employment balance," Riada economist Padraic Garvey said. "So the overall balance was not as bad as expected."
Dealers said Friday's U.S. payrolls data was the main focus this week and would give a better indication of how the economy was performing.

Closer to home the resignation of a government minister, triggered by concerns over financial irregularities, caused a ripple of uncertainty as further reverberations were likely before the matter was concluded satisfactorily.
"Political upheaval is never good for the market and there is some small concern that this may rock the boat for the coalition," a dealer said.
